hero.title: Riverdale Community Center: From Bulletin Board to Every Pocket
hero.intro: For twenty years, Riverdale Community Center ran on word of mouth and Sunday announcements. The work was strong. The reach wasffddsdn't. This demo page shows how inline editing feels on a rddddddeal story layout.

background.heading: Background
paragraphs: Maria Santos didn't meet the board at a gala. She met them in the parking lot after a Saturday food drive, hauling boxes alongside volunteers who had been showing up for years. By the time any technology conversation happened, the trust was already there.

The center had been serving Riverdale for two decades. But community awareness had quietly narrowed. Families who used services three years ago didn't know about new evening classes. Donors who gave once couldn't find a path back in. Nobody made that decision intentionally — the channels just didn't follow people home.

challenge.heading: The Challenge
paragraphs: Most community organizations run on three channels: word of mouth, partner announcements, and a website people visit only when they already know to look.

That's not a criticism. It's structural. Every channel requires someone to already be looking. A neighbor who heard the name once isn't looking. A parent who needs after-school programming isn't looking, because they don't know it exists.
challenge.callout: None of those channels follow someone home.
challenge.afterStats: The gap isn't motivation — it's presence. People live on their phones. Most community centers just aren't there yet in a way that feels owned, branded, and easy to update without calling a developer.

approach.heading: Our Approach
paragraphs: We built a branded mobile experience the center could run themselves: events, push updates, program listings, and volunteer sign-ups — managed in minutes, not sprint cycles.
What the community sees is Riverdale. Their colors, their programs, their voice. What staff get is something they can actually maintain without a computer science degree.

result.heading: The Result
paragraphs: The pilot launched in six weeks. Early metrics are promising: repeat visits up, event sign-ups smoother, and staff spending less time answering the same questions by phone.

impact.heading: Why It Matters
paragraphs: Most nonprofit leaders aren't short on mission. What's hard to find is a way to experiment without betting the annual budget on custom engineering.
Riverdale didn't have to. They got a credible digital front door and a team that could keep it current — for a fraction of what bespoke development would havefdsffdsa cost.
